page: Microsoft Azure E8-4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with a constrained core count to provide high memory density per thread. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.35 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a high 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 16 MB of L3 cache, a 32 KB L1 data cache, and a 0.5 MB L2 cache.

Storage configuration includes a 137 GB local solid-state drive suitable for paging files, transient caches, and temporary data sets. The instance lacks dedicated GPU acceleration and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. On the architectural level, the x86_64 CPU supports standard extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but does not provide AVX-512 or AMX acceleration.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, recording 2706.38 in stress-ng single-core tests. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity is constrained by the 4-vCPU limit, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core result of 5408.28 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3667.0. Memory throughput reaches 39.48 GB/sec on large read blocks and 257.26 GB/sec on cached reads, yielding a PassMark memory score of 2543.95. Network-facing and intensive transactional benchmarks yield modest throughput, including 4.07 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.93 GB/sec in static web serving.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-4as_v4 serves workloads where software licensing depends on core counts but memory capacity demands are substantial. Rather than paying for surplus CPU cores to obtain 64 GB of RAM, this configuration curtails licensing costs. It is well-suited for medium-scale in-memory caches, relational database systems like MySQL or PostgreSQL requiring ample buffer pools, and ETL data ingestion tasks.

Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system includes 137 GB of local SSD storage and features a 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core performance alongside balanced uncached memory read bandwidth of 39.48 GB/sec, though aggregate multi-core computational throughput is bound by its core count.
